frames.observation: Abyssal Crown is fully framed before the native pass. The authored teal crown shell, colored spikes, side eye details and lower rigid eye insert form a readable low-poly silhouette; the player action panel covers only the foreground hero.

The custom crown remains centered and coherent in krakenIdle after the action panel closes. The separate rigid eye insert remains aligned beneath the larger animated shell, and no native replacement mesh is visible.
A later settled krakenIdle sample preserves the complete shell, spikes, side details and eye insert at native scale. The model occupies the enemy cell without clipping the room boundary.

At the native Attack trigger boundary, camera and transition blur overlap the crown. Its full silhouette and eye insert remain recognizable, but the blur prevents fine edge or surface judgment in this frame.
The opening of krakenAttack lifts the shell above a bright native ground burst. The authored geometry stays connected and the lower eye insert remains aligned, while the glow masks the underside.

During krakenAttack, the crown rises and extends a tall decorated teal column toward the player. The shell, side details and eye insert remain coherent, although the top of the enlarged pose approaches the HUD.

The extended attack pose remains structurally intact behind bright pink native effects. The upper shell is partly outside the camera frame, so this sample supports motion continuity but not a complete silhouette review.
A large native impact flare covers most of the attacking model. The visible teal column remains continuous, but this frame cannot establish the hidden shell surface or eye alignment.
The crown has returned to its compact silhouette while native RESIST UP text and rings cross the shell. All authored components are again aligned, though the overlay limits color inspection.
The pass capture ends in krakenIdle with the full custom crown and lower eye insert intact. Enemy HP remains 324 and the hero remains at 999 HP.
The ordinary zero-focus hammer attempt begins with Abyssal Crown fully visible at 324 HP. The custom shell and rigid eye insert retain the same placement seen in the pass capture.
Immediately before impact, the crown remains stable in krakenIdle and the full authored silhouette is unobstructed. The attack roll UI overlaps only the foreground.

The ordinary hammer impact coincides with the native Damaged trigger and the HP display changes to 316. A bright impact sphere and the hero obscure most of the crown, so the event boundary is clear but the complete hit pose is not.
The native 8-damage label appears while the impact sphere still covers much of the model. Visible crown edges remain connected, but foreground overlap prevents a full krakenDamage pose judgment.
Early krakenDamage is visible behind the hero with the 8-damage label. The shell has compressed and shifted without tearing; the foreground hero masks the lower insert and central surface.
Late krakenDamage has restored the crown near its centered shape at 316 HP. The authored spikes, side details and lower eye insert are all readable again.
The hit response is nearly complete and the custom crown holds a coherent centered silhouette. No detached skin, stretched spike or native mesh appears.
At the end of the krakenDamage transition, the model is visually restored to its original compact pose at 316 HP. The eye insert remains registered under the head.
The next player decision opens with Abyssal Crown intact at 316 HP in krakenIdle. The action UI covers the hero but leaves the complete enemy silhouette visible.
The attack capture ends with the exact custom crown still settled in krakenIdle at 316 HP. This frame confirms recovery after the ordinary nonlethal hit, not another attack outcome.
The explicit KillSingle fixture begins with the exact custom crown intact at 316 HP. This is a separate fixture-death sequence and the selection panel covers only the hero.
Immediately before the fixture strike, Abyssal Crown remains fully visible and coherent in krakenIdle at 316 HP.

The telemetry-selected native Death trigger coincides with a large impact sphere, red screen tint and foreground hero. The custom model is mostly obscured, so this frame establishes the fixture boundary but not the disappearance pose.
The native 1000-damage label appears while the impact sphere still covers the center. Visible crown edges and spikes remain authored geometry, but the effects prevent complete surface inspection.

Early krakenDisappear collapses and lowers the crown behind the hero. The visible shell, spike and eye details remain connected while the animation removes the model; this is animator-driven motion because the source reports m_DoRagdoll false.

The custom crown is no longer visible in the camera while telemetry continues to report the same active renderer playing krakenDisappear. This image establishes visual removal in the sampled view, not object destruction or general cleanup timing.

Combat UI has cleared and the crown remains absent from the sampled camera view while the bounded krakenDisappear telemetry continues. The dungeon objective update does not prove final renderer disposal.

The camera begins settling on the cleared room and no crown geometry is visible. Telemetry still retains the exact active renderer in krakenDisappear, so this frame is limited to camera-visible disappearance.
The cleared room remains free of visible crown geometry as the camera continues to settle. This bounded image does not establish cleanup causality.
The late retained prefix still shows a cleared room with no visible crown. The exact renderer remains active in telemetry through frame 89, so absence from the image is not claimed as destruction.

The final retained frame presents the native Ready prompt over the cleared room. Telemetry reports the same renderer inactive and not visible at this frame; the next sample encountered renderer destruction, which proves only the recorded teardown boundary.

requirements: All 31 referenced original PNGs were inspected before assigning the reviewed status.
Every observation is scoped to the exact frame and its telemetry boundary.
The exact source is directEnemy krakenHead, CEL enKraken(Clone), motion renderer kraken2 and source renderer 121035. No inheritance is granted to another Kraken source or renderer topology.

The same-owner rigid companion at Root_M/base/body/neck/eye/kraken2_eye was separately bound as MeshRenderer instance -245412 with abyssal-crown-kraken-eye-v4.glb. It is preserved as required profile context and receives no skinned topology or motion credit.

The native pass preserved enemy HP 324 and hero HP 999. Its sampled CharacterDummy action records AttackProf with Attack override, proficiency 288 success, damage 0 and HarmlessAttack, with both recorded actor and victim FIDs belonging to the Kraken. It does not prove hero damage or ordinary Kraken encounter balance.

One ordinary zero-focus native hammer attack reduced Abyssal Crown from 324 to 316 HP with recorded damage 8, a Damaged response and krakenDamage. This is the required ordinary nonlethal hit evidence.
The explicit KillSingle fixture reduced Abyssal Crown from 316 to 0 HP with recorded damage 1000 and a Death response. It is fixture death evidence, not ordinary lethal gameplay.

The source reports m_DoRagdoll false and zero rigidbodies. The animator remains enabled while krakenDisappear plays from frame 29 through frame 89 of the death capture, so the disappearance is animated rather than ragdoll motion.

Exact renderer instance -245368, owner 369188, CEL -245362, path kraken2, mesh and bone signature remain unchanged through all 331 retained telemetry frames. It is active, enabled and reported visible through death frame 89; frame 90 retains the identity with enabled true, active false and visible false.

The kill capture retained 91 of 120 requested frames and then terminated with renderer_destroyed. The prefix proves the sampled animated disappearance and the inactive final retained boundary, but it does not prove cleanup causality, full post-death lifetime or behavior beyond the next missing sample.
Strict Ready succeeded after combat at dungeon level 0, room 2, with one active Ready button. No Loot Collect vote was present or submitted in this route.
The Standard matKraken material on the selected motion renderer uses abyssal-crown-kraken-head-v2.png as its main texture with emission disabled, zero emission color and no emission map.

Native effects, foreground hero overlap, attack camera movement, UI and the tall attack pose limit inspection in stated frames. The captures do not establish portrait pixels, all-angle culling, collision, general cleanup timing, final disposal or finished-art acceptance.
